newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian rial gains on lower demand for hard cash.
newsitem.headline: Iranian rial gains on lower demand for hard cash.

text.p: The Iranian rial has gained about six percent against the dollar in the past few weeks on lower demand for hard currencies, money dealers said on Thursday.
London-based Iranian trader Ali Pakpour said his firm was selling dollars at up to 4,630 rials each in Europe, compared to 4,930 in late November.
The German mark sold for 2,820 rials, the pound sterling for 7,770 rials and the French franc for 830 rials, he said.
In, Dubai, a major trading post for Iranian private and state firms, one dollar cost 4,650 rials, a dealer said.
One Tehran resident said the dollar traded at about 4,600 rials on the black market.
Some dealers attributed the drop to a crackdown by security forces on the black market in Iran.

"There has been a strong drop in demand because a lot of dealers and businessmen have been arrested in the past two months," Pakpour said. "We (dealers) are more careful now and the buyers are more careful too."
But a trader in Dubai said the drop in demand was probably more due to people using their money in a variety of schemes introduced by the government to pay in advance for homes and telephones.

Iran banned free currency exchange in May 1995, setting an official rate of 3,000 rials to the dollar. The moved followed a drop in the value of the currency to 7,000 per dollar after Washington announced a trade and investment ban against Tehran.
The move led to relative stability of the rial's exchange rate after police and security agents arrested hundreds of illegal money changers, pushing the black market underground.
